routeChoiceRationale: The stripe reconstruction has exactly 2 routes (/ and /industries/media-entertainment). The homepage was chosen: it is the multi-column, carousel-heavy, breakpoint-dense route and the canonical landing surface.

baselineClassWhy.700: Below the 915 subtree breakpoint, so the mobile subtree renders; it is frozen at its 390 capture width, so the entire page renders as a 390px column inside a 700px viewport with ~310px (44%) of dead right gutter for its full 20,349px height (source is 14,831px). Pathological whitespace.
baselineClassWhy.1100: Desktop subtree frozen at the 1440 truth width: scrollWidth 1440 vs innerWidth 1100, 142 overflowing nodes, every section clipped at the right edge, and 37 chars of normal-flow content (the cookie banner's 'Reject all' / 'manage cookies' controls) pushed past the right edge and unreachable.
baselineClassWhy.1440: Truth width. Matches the source on every metric that matters (offscreen 322 vs source 327 nodes, 991 vs 991 offscreen chars, all of it inside horizontally scrollable carousel tracks, 0 chars lost from normal flow, no horizontal overflow).

patchedClassWhy.700: Unchanged. Byte-identical screenshot and byte-identical metrics to baseline: the mechanism only touches the desktop subtree, and 700 renders the mobile subtree. Same residual agent D reported for linear.
patchedClassWhy.1100: IMPROVED from BLOCKER. Page overflow halves (scrollWidth 1440 -> 1271), overflowing nodes 142 -> 93, and the 37 normal-flow chars lost at baseline are recovered (flow-offscreen chars 37 -> 0). Text reflows correctly (paragraphs rewrap). Still MAJOR because ~171px of horizontal overflow remains: frozen px survives deeper in the tree, exactly the residual agent D measured on linear.
patchedClassWhy.1440: REGRESSED from MINOR. No content is lost (normal-flow offscreen chars stay 0) but the page's centered container is unfrozen with max-width:none, so the left/right gutters collapse (contentMinLeft 0 -> -56) and every section spans wider than the source. Carousel tracks widen too (offscreen chars 991 -> 2377, all still inside horizontal scrollers, i.e. reachable). Visible, uniform fidelity loss at the width that was previously exact.

patchedNoMaxWidthWhy.1100: Same improvement as the full patch, and slightly better: overflowing nodes 142 -> 79 (vs 93), scrollWidth 1440 -> 1271, flow-offscreen chars 37 -> 0, carousel offscreen chars stay at the baseline level (1106 vs 1099) instead of doubling.
patchedNoMaxWidthWhy.1440: Back to baseline: contentMinLeft 0, contentMaxRight 6207 (= baseline), overflowing 24 (baseline 26, source 25), offscreen chars 1038 (baseline/source 991), 0 normal-flow chars lost, screenshot visually identical to baseline. Regression eliminated.

bandsClampedNote: ZERO. The stripe reconstruction contains no synthetic hidden bands at all: manifest layout.responsiveHidden == 0 and generated-styles.css (9.0 MB) contains 0 occurrences of '@media'. The band-clamp half of the mechanism is a provable no-op on this site - it can neither help nor hurt. The patch script ran unmodified and reported bandsRewritten: 0.

regressionDetail.answer: YES, at 1440 only, for the mechanism exactly as agent D emitted it. NO at 1100 (large improvement) and NO at 700 (bit-identical).
regressionDetail.cause: The unfreeze rule emits `width:auto !important; max-width:none !important`. The `max-width:none` half is unjustified: the frozen style atom's max-width is the source's own computed max-width, so discarding it always destroys a real authored cap. Stripe's page shell is a centered container with a max-width plus side padding; it grows between 1024 and 1440, is therefore correctly detected as fluid, and then loses its cap - so at and above 1440 the gutters collapse. Linear never exposed this because its detection pair was 1440/1920, where its cap was already binding at both samples.
regressionDetail.fixVerified: Dropping `max-width:none` and emitting only `width:auto` (variant patched-nomaxwidth, port 4752) removes the 1440 regression completely while keeping the entire 1100 gain, and is in fact slightly better at 1100 than the original. Measured, not argued.
regressionDetail.destructiveNote: Even in the regressing variant, normal-flow offscreen text stayed 0 at every width. All offscreen text on this page - in the source too - lives inside horizontally scrollable carousel tracks, so the raw offscreenTextChars metric is misleading on stripe; the discriminating metric is offscreen text in NORMAL FLOW.

linearSpecificDependencies.detail: agent-d/scripts/patch-c3.mjs and patch-c.mjs ran on stripe with zero code edits - only the spec dir and the two probe widths are arguments. The [data-wr-page]/[data-wr-viewport]/[data-wr-node] scoping, the style-catalog shape and the probe arrays were all identical. 0 unmatched selectors, 0 assumption failures.

Fires only when the generator actually synthesized responsive-hidden bands. Linear /pricing had 738; stripe has 0. So half the winning mechanism delivered nothing here. It is not linear-specific in design, but its VALUE was linear-specific.

linearSpecificDependencies.verdict: NOT self-determining - the one real external dependency
linearSpecificDependencies.detail: Fluidity detection needs two probe widths both above the site's top AUTHORED layout switch. Linear's is 1024 -> pair (1440,1920), which found only 9 fluid nodes. Stripe's is 940 -> pair (1024,1440), which finds 782 on the homepage; the (1440,1920) pair would have found only 28. Getting this wrong is precisely what produces false-fluid detection. It cannot be read from the IR: stripe's observation carries authoredLayout on 0 of 2280 elements.

linearSpecificDependencies.verdict: generalizes - confirmed on a second site
linearSpecificDependencies.detail: All 8 of stripe.com's stylesheets throw on cssRules in-page (readableInPage 0/8), yet all 8 fetch fine directly, yielding 379 @media width conditions and a clean top switch at 940 (min-width:940 in 108 rules, max-width:939 in 11). This is the same defect agent D flagged as a separate high-value bug on linear, now reproduced on stripe.

700 is untouched on stripe for the same reason as on linear: generateLayoutCss runs only for the desktop subtree, so the mobile subtree stays frozen at its 390 capture. It is the single largest residual on stripe's homepage (a 390px column in a 700px viewport).

generalizes.verdict: YES, WITH ONE MANDATORY CORRECTION AND ONE REQUIRED INPUT
generalizes.rationale: The generic algorithm ran on a second, structurally unrelated site with no code changes and no selector assumptions failing, and it converted stripe's 1100 from BLOCKER to MAJOR (page overflow halved, the only normal-flow content loss recovered) while leaving 700 bit-identical. It is not free of risk: as agent D emitted it, it also regressed the 1440 truth width by discarding authored max-width caps - a defect linear's probe pair happened to mask - and dropping the unjustified `max-width:none` declaration removes that regression entirely while keeping the full gain, verified by measurement. The band-clamp half is a no-op on any site the generator did not synthesize hidden bands for, so the fluid-unfreeze half is the part that carries the generalization.
requiredCorrections: Emit `width:auto` only. NEVER emit `max-width:none`: the frozen atom's max-width is the source's own computed cap and discarding it destroys real layout at and above the truth width.
requiredInputs: The site's top authored layout switch, used to pick the two probe widths. Recover it by fetching every stylesheet href directly (in-page cssRules is CORS-blocked on both sites tested) and histogramming @media width conditions. On stripe this is 940, so the usable pair on the shipped 5-width probe is (1024,1440) - no re-observation needed, unlike linear.
residualsThatDoNotGeneralizeAway: The mobile subtree stays frozen at its capture width (700 is a BLOCKER on stripe, before and after).
Frozen px deeper in the tree keeps ~171px of horizontal overflow at 1100.
